visual.description: Two proportional circles showing massive PFAS difference. Left: tiny circle for Cotton-Polyester Blend (1.7 ng/g, Accent Blue). Right: massive circle for 100% Cotton Uniforms (19,100 ng/g, Accent Pink). The cotton circle dwarfs the blend circle — area-proportional sqrt scaling. Title: 'PFAS in School Uniforms'. Label below: '11,000× difference' in JetBrains Mono. Annotation: 'Stain-resistant finish is the culprit' in Inter. Small note: '6:2 FTOH up to 153,000 ng/g in some samples'.
visual.sourceText: Source: Xia et al., Environ. Sci. Technol., 2022

dataChart.title: PFAS in Children's School Uniforms
dataChart.annotation: 11,000× difference — stain-resistant FINISH is the culprit, not the fiber

notes: This is one of the most dramatic scale comparisons in the video. The 11,000x difference makes the small circle almost invisible next to the large one. The paradox — 100% cotton being worse — is the key takeaway. This same comparison will callback in scene-024. Crossfade into BPA section.
